finding: Under the stated conditions (the Giza dwell, fully developed speckle, no reference image, no receiver noise, one room-specific motion pattern coherent for the whole pass, at its worst phase), a detection at 95% with 5% false alarms needs at least these room-specific line-of-sight amplitudes, exactly within the model: 3.02 mm at 0.2 Hz over a footprint of 279 m^2 (3.03 mm over 4.4 m^2); 47.3 um at 80 Hz over 279 m^2 (379 um over 4.4 m^2). The bench room's modelled static imprint under Giza's regional microseism level falls short of the curve at its own footprint by 8.3e8; its dynamic imprints under a truck over a bump 15 m away for the whole pass by 1.4e2 to 1.1e3. A mechanism that only changes the ambient motion's phase (any phase change moves the ground by at most twice the ambient amplitude, linear or not) or scatters it as P2-26's rooms do (at most 2.36 times), would need the ambient levels here raised at least 1.9e1 times. Handing the method the ground's reflectivity lowers the curve; a corner reflector on the footprint's peak needs 14 um whatever the footprint. These are requirements conditional on the model: they say nothing of routes outside it, nor of mechanisms not specified.
